name: Berchta
description: Berchta (also Perchta) is an Alpine Germanic supernatural figure associated with the Twelve Days of Christmas and Epiphany, manifesting in dual form as a beautiful white-robed woman or a haggard old crone, rewarding industrious households and punishing the idle with gruesome evisceration.

aliases.name: Perchta
aliases.meaning: The bright one / the bearer — from Old High German 'beraht' (bright, shining)

aliases.name: Frau Faste
aliases.meaning: Lady Fasting — connected to the Feast of Epiphany and Shrovetide

aliases.name: Pehta
aliases.meaning: Slovenian name for the same figure

aliases.name: Berchtentag
aliases.meaning: Berchta's Day — the feast of Epiphany (January 6), on which Perchta/Berchta was particularly active

origin: Berchta tradition is concentrated in the Alpine Germanic cultural zone: southern Bavaria, Austria (especially Tyrol, Salzburg, Carinthia), Switzerland, and Slovenia. The figure is absent or much diminished in northern Germany.
